applicationPortal.value: Apply online through SFCM's application portal. SFCM's Application and Auditions page says the page guides applicants through application and audition requirements, and the Piano program page confirms a Graduate Master of Music in Piano. Required application materials vary by program and can include the application fee, degree prerequisites, transcripts, test scores, essays, recommendation letters, and prescreening materials. Graduate and postgraduate applicants must submit transcripts from all colleges or universities attended. All applicants must submit two recommendation letters through the recommendation form linked in the application.

applicationFee.value: Application fee: $100 non-refundable, payable by credit or debit card, required to officially submit the SFCM application. Automatic fee waiver or reduction: current and previous SFCM students receive a full fee waiver; Denis de Coteau Fellowship applicants receive a full fee waiver; qualifying event participants receive a $50 discount. Fee waiver request deadlines: December 1 for Fall entry and October 15 for Spring entry. Enrollment deposit after acceptance: $500 non-refundable, credited toward the first semester bill.

auditionRequirements.value: Piano is a prescreened area. All piano applicants who advance to the final round are required to audition in person on campus in San Francisco. Applicants unable to attend a live audition may request an alternative format on a case-by-case basis for all programs except Artist Diploma; if approved, they must submit final audition recordings of all required repertoire and complete a live Zoom audition with faculty. Recorded audition notes: final recorded auditions for graduate and professional studies certificate applicants are available upon request once the scheduling module opens; recorded auditions may require a Zoom interview with the piano area; all recordings must be audiovisual. General audition policy: virtual audition requests open when live audition scheduling opens in mid-December, and video auditions are due February 15 if the request is approved. Fall 2026 Piano audition dates listed by SFCM: February 13, 14, 15, 16, 23, and 27.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: Graduate applicants must submit at least 30 minutes of recordings. Prescreening repertoire: One Allegro movement of a Classical period sonata. Prescreening repertoire: One work from the Romantic era; individual movements from larger works are acceptable. Prescreening repertoire: One etude of virtuosity by Chopin, Liszt, Rachmaninoff, Scriabin, Debussy, Prokofiev, Stravinsky, Bartok, or Ligeti. Prescreening repertoire: Additional contrasting works may be included to fulfill the minimum time requirement. Final audition repertoire: Graduate applicants must have at least 50 minutes of repertoire. Final audition repertoire: One complete Classical work by Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven, or Schubert. Final audition repertoire: One etude of virtuosity by Chopin, Liszt, Rachmaninoff, Scriabin, Debussy, Prokofiev, Stravinsky, Bartok, or Ligeti. Final audition repertoire: Two additional works or movements of contrasting style. Additional repertoire notes: all repertoire must be performed from memory except Contemporary selections. Additional repertoire notes: multi-movement works may be uploaded in separate audiovisual files; include the name of the piece or movement at the beginning of the recording and/or in the uploaded description. Additional repertoire notes: SFCM encourages applicants to include one work composed by a woman and/or person from a historically underrepresented racial or ethnic group. Additional repertoire notes: current SFCM students are not required to submit a prescreening except Artist Diploma applicants, but all current SFCM students must upload the video essay.

deadlines.value: Fall 2026 status as of May 24, 2026: SFCM states that the Fall 2026 application has closed, but late applications are being accepted on a case-by-case basis through the Late Application Request Form. SFCM says it is not accepting late applications for the following piano studios: Garrick Ohlsson, Awadagin Pratt, and Jon Nakamatsu. Regular application deadline: December 1, 2025. Extended application deadline: December 3, 2025. Prescreening decisions released on a rolling basis: beginning December 16, 2025. All prescreening decisions released: December 19, 2025. Recommendation letters due and audition self-scheduling closes: January 15, 2026. Assisted audition scheduling: January 16-31, 2026. Live and remote auditions: February 2026. Video auditions due if approved: February 15, 2026. Piano audition dates: February 13, 14, 15, 16, 23, and 27, 2026. Admission decisions with merit scholarship offers: March 16-20, 2026. All full financial aid offers released: April 1, 2026. Graduate and postgraduate applicant response deadline: April 15, 2026.

englishScores.value: Applicability: all international applicants whose native language is not English must submit an in-person/testing center TOEFL or IELTS score; U.S. permanent residents whose native language is not English must undergo ELP waiver-form review to determine whether they must submit TOEFL or IELTS. Accepted tests: TOEFL iBT at a testing center, SFCM school code 4744; IELTS at a testing center. Minimum scores for Master of Music: TOEFL iBT 80; IELTS 6.5. Not accepted: Duolingo and TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted. Score date validation for Fall 2026: SFCM does not accept TOEFL or IELTS scores dated before September 1, 2024. Temporary scores: TOEFL iBT Home Edition and IELTS Academic Online at Home may be uploaded with the application as temporary scores, but official in-person/testing-center scores must be sent by March 1 for Fall applicants. If scores do not meet the minimum or sub-scores vary notably, applicants may be required to complete a 10-15 minute ELP Assessment Interview. Applicants admitted on TOEFL/IELTS probation must submit new passing scores by May 1 for Fall entry. All enrolling students whose native language is not English complete an English diagnostic/placement exam at Orientation.

applicationPortal.value: Apply online through SFCM's application portal. SFCM's Collaborative Piano program page confirms a Graduate Collaborative Piano Master of Music and states that the graduate-level degree track is offered to a few select students. Required application materials vary by program and can include the application fee, degree prerequisites, transcripts, test scores, essays, recommendation letters, and audition materials. Graduate and postgraduate applicants must submit transcripts from all colleges or universities attended. All applicants must submit two recommendation letters through the recommendation form linked in the application.

Fee waiver request deadlines: December 1 for Fall entry and October 15 for Spring entry. Enrollment deposit after acceptance: $500 non-refundable, credited toward the first semester bill.

auditionRequirements.value: Collaborative Piano is a non-prescreened area. Live auditions are held on campus in San Francisco. If applicants are unable to attend in person, virtual auditions by video recording are available upon request once the audition scheduling module opens. Collaborative Piano applicants audition with SFCM students and may not bring their own soloists. For the final audition, applicants are required to perform with the vocalist and violinist provided by SFCM. General audition policy: virtual audition requests open when live audition scheduling opens in mid-December, and video auditions are due February 15 if the request is approved. Fall 2026 Collaborative Piano audition dates listed by SFCM: February 13 and February 22.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: There is no prescreening requirement for Collaborative Piano applicants. Final audition repertoire: Applicants must prepare two complete major solo works; one must be composed by a woman and/or person from a historically underrepresented racial or ethnic group. Final audition repertoire: Applicants must prepare one complete instrumental sonata chosen from Beethoven: Violin Sonata No. 5 in F Major or Brahms: Violin Sonata No. 2 in A Major. Final audition repertoire: Applicants must prepare four vocal pieces chosen from Strauss: Allerseelen; Barber: The Monk and His Cat; Brahms: Meine Liebe ist Grün; Schubert: Ganymed; Debussy: C'est l'extase; Puccini: Mi chiamano Mimi. Additional repertoire notes: for the final audition, applicants are required to perform with the vocalist and violinist provided by SFCM. Additional repertoire notes: collaborative piano applicants audition with SFCM students and may not bring their own soloists.
